reason: Confirmed in @carbon/react 1.117: arrow keys are handled only by the menu items and the `ul` (`OverflowMenu.js` line 278), and `FloatingMenu` focuses the first entry only in an effect after placement (`FloatingMenu.js` lines 150-156). So an ArrowDown pressed right after Enter reaches the trigger, which ignores it. The new TC-003 test (`tests/leboncoin-session-settings.spec.ts` lines 622-624) can then open Information instead of Settings, which is the same load-dependent race this issue is meant to remove. It also contradicts the new FR-APP-MENU-007 corner case, "keys pressed in quick succession give the same result as the same keys pressed slowly".
`tests/app-information.spec.ts` line 378 behaves as intended: the `for` body is the single Tab press, and `await close()` runs once after the loop. Only the formatting is misleading.
title: Put `await close()` on its own line in the TC-007 Information modal test
todo:
**Problem:** In `tests/app-information.spec.ts` line 378, the Tab loop and `await close();` are on one line, separated by stray spaces: `for (...) await page.keyboard.press("Tab");      await close();`. This makes `close()` look like part of the loop body.

**Suggested work:** Move `await close();` to its own line after the loop, at the same indentation. Do not change behaviour.
